stories.title: Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater
stories.excerpt: The Trust for Gov­er­nors Island has released a Request for Expres­sions of Inter­est (RFEI) for the revi­tal­iza­tion of two his­toric build­ings on the Island, Build­ing 324 and Build­ing 330. The RFEI invites ideas from prospec­tive part­ners for the revi­tal­iza­tion of these his­toric assets, bring­ing them back into active, year-round use. The Trust seeks respons­es that pro­pose arts and cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, or oth­er pub­lic-fac­ing uses. The two adja­cent build­ings are locat­ed with­in the Gov­er­nors Island His­toric Dis­trict. Orig­i­nal­ly con­struct­ed as a YMCA recre­ation cen­ter and a movie the­ater, respec­tive­ly, the build­ings fea­ture high ceil­ings and open floor plans. “The for­mer YMCA and Fort Jay The­ater his­tor­i­cal­ly stood as cul­tur­al anchors of Gov­er­nors Island, and we’re thrilled to present a unique oppor­tu­ni­ty to breathe new life into these icon­ic build­ings,” said Clare New­man, pres­i­dent and CEO of the Trust for Gov­er­nors Island. ​“We’re seek­ing vision­ary part­ners with bold ideas for cul­tur­al, recre­ation­al, and pub­lic-fac­ing uses that can turn untapped poten­tial into vibrant spaces for every­one to enjoy.” The com­plete RFEI can be viewed here. Submissions are due by Oct. 26. The post Governors Island Issues RFEI for Revitalization of Former YMCA, Theater appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trust for Governors Island RFEIs two historic buildings (former YMCA, theater) for revitalization.
Submissions due October 26; seeks arts, cultural, recreational, public-facing uses.
High ceilings and open floor plans in Buildings 324 and 330.
stories.summary: The Trust for Governors Island has issued an RFEI for adaptive reuse of two historic buildings on the island—a former YMCA recreation center and movie theater—seeking proposals for cultural, recreational, or public-facing uses. The buildings feature high ceilings and open floor plans conducive to flexible programming. Submissions are due by October 26.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Governors Island's reuse as cultural/recreational venues (not residential) does not create housing demand. However, if successful revitalization attracts year-round residency and workforce to the island, it could signal future demand for residential infill—worth monitoring for longer-term mixed-use opportunity.

stories.title: 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced that Deferred, the first and only technology-powered qualified intermediary transforming 1031 exchanges for everyday real estate investors, has joined Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program as a provider of 1031 exchange solutions. The relationship is designed to provide Marcus & Millichap’s clients with streamlined access to qualified intermediary services and technology-enabled 1031 exchange solutions. As interest rates, tax considerations, and market conditions continue to influence investment decisions, many commercial real estate owners seek ways to maximize after-tax proceeds while maintaining purchasing power. Through this relationship, Marcus & Millichap’s clients will gain access to Deferred’s exchange platform, educational resources, and experienced exchange professionals. “1031 exchanges remain one of the most effective tools available to investors seeking to preserve equity and reposition capital,” said Richard Matricaria, chief growth officer of Marcus & Millichap. “Deferred provides a modern, client-focused approach to guiding investors through the exchange process. Their combination of expertise, service and technology makes them a valuable addition to our Preferred Partner Program.” The post 1031 Exchange Solutions Provider Joins Marcus & Millichap’s Preferred Partner Program appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Deferred joins Marcus & Millichap Preferred Partner Program for 1031 exchange services.
Technology-enabled qualified intermediary streamlines exchange process for commercial real estate investors.
Rising interest rates and tax considerations drive investor appetite for capital redeployment tools.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap announced that Deferred, a technology-powered qualified intermediary, has joined its Preferred Partner Program to provide clients with streamlined 1031 exchange solutions. The partnership offers clients access to Deferred's exchange platform, educational resources, and experienced professionals. Higher interest rates and tax considerations are prompting more investors to explore ways to preserve equity and reposition capital.
stories.impact: Signals strong capital mobility demand among commercial real estate investors facing higher financing costs. Easier access to 1031 exchanges via technology may accelerate portfolio repositioning and tax-deferred reinvestment into multifamily, particularly for operators seeking to rotate out of higher-cap-rate or overvalued assets into new ground-up development or lower-cap markets.

stories.title: Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty
stories.excerpt: Greystone has provided a total of $91,851,000 in Fannie Mae loans to refinance and acquire three affordable housing communities located in New York. The financing was originated by senior managing director Eric Rosenstock and EVP Jeff Englund on behalf of Metropolitan Realty Group. The financing includes three affordable multifamily communities that will each undergo moderate rehabilitation as part of the transaction. Built in 1975, Pine Town Houses is a 130-unit garden-style apartment community in Long Beach, NY. Hudson View II and III, in Northern Manhattan’s Hamilton Heights neighborhood, total 129 apartments and 11 commercial spaces. Ariel Property Advisors recently arranged the Hudson View II and III acquisition. Each non-recourse, fixed-rate Fannie Mae loan features a 10-year term with five years of interest-only payments, followed by a 35-year amortization schedule. All three properties are supported by long-term Section 8 Housing Assistance Payments (HAP) contracts and are subject to long-term affordability restrictions.  The post Greystone Provides $92M in Fannie Mae Loans to Metropolitan Realty appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greystone arranged $91.85M Fannie Mae refinance/acquisition loans for Metropolitan Realty Group.
Three affordable NYC multifamily properties: 130-unit Pine Town Houses (Long Beach), 129-unit Hudson View II/III (Hamilton Heights, Manhattan).
Non-recourse fixed-rate loans, 10-year terms with 5-year IO, backed by long-term Section 8 HAP contracts.
stories.summary: Greystone originated $91.85 million in Fannie Mae non-recourse loans for Metropolitan Realty Group to refinance and acquire three affordable multifamily communities in New York: Pine Town Houses (130 units, Long Beach) and Hudson View II/III (129 units plus 11 commercial spaces, Hamilton Heights). Each property will undergo moderate rehabilitation and benefits from long-term Section 8 HAP contracts and affordability restrictions. Loans feature fixed rates, 10-year terms with 5 years of interest-only payments.
stories.impact: Demonstrates sustained Fannie Mae appetite for workforce/affordable multifamily in NY metros despite higher rates, particularly when backed by durable Section 8 income. For developers: affordable acquisition-plus-rehab remains financeable in outer-borough NYC submarkets (Long Beach, Hamilton Heights), signaling continued capital availability for value-add repositioning of stabilized rent-restricted stock with long-term payment guarantees.

stories.title: E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center
stories.excerpt: E Ink, an originator, pioneer and global commercial leader in ePaper technology, broke ground on the expansion of its U.S. headquarters in Billerica, MA. The project expands the footprint at the company’s Billerica Innovation Center, which is home to 260-plus E Ink employees and serves as a key global R&D center. “Expanding our Billerica campus strengthens our ability to advance technology innovation in the United States, support our customers around the world, and contribute to the continued growth of the local economy and innovation community,” said Paul Apen, chief business and operations officer at E Ink Construction is expected to be completed by March 2027 with support from NV5 Planning & Design, Inc., IF Design L.L.C., and SPEC Process Engineering & Construction, Inc.E Ink was spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 1997 and has been headquartered in Billerica since its inception. The post E Ink Breaks Ground on Expansion of Billerica Innovation Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: E Ink breaks ground on expansion of Billerica, MA U.S. headquarters and R&D center.
260+ employees at site; expansion completion targeted for March 2027.
Signals continued growth and R&D investment in advanced materials/technology sector in Boston metro.
stories.summary: E Ink, the ePaper technology pioneer headquartered in Billerica, MA since 1997, has broken ground on an expansion of its U.S. Innovation Center campus, which currently houses 260+ employees and serves as a global R&D hub. Construction is expected to complete by March 2027. The expansion reflects the company's strategy to strengthen innovation capacity and support customer growth.
stories.impact: Signals sustained employer investment in Boston-area life sciences/advanced manufacturing. E Ink's headcount and campus expansion suggest growing specialized workforce demand in Billerica and surrounding Route 128 corridor. For multifamily developers: increased demand signals opportunity to target young R&D talent housing (studios to 2BR, modern amenities, proximity to transit/campus) in Billerica and inner-ring suburbs; monitor for 2026–2027 absorption surge as expansion nears completion.

stories.title: Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus
stories.excerpt: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer announced a joint investment in a $90-million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed, 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego. The borrower, Gemdale USA, will use the proceeds to refinance an existing loan. The four-building lab and office campus in Del Mar Heights is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences, a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to discovering, developing and commercializing life-changing treatments for patients with under-addressed neurological, psychiatric, endocrine and immunological disorders. Aperture Del Mar serves as Neurocrine’s mission-critical global headquarters as part of a lease that runs through 2036. The loan is part of Breakthrough’s second life science fund, which held its first close at the end of 2025. Tishman Speyer participated through its recently established debt platform. Breakthrough is a joint venture of Tishman Speyer and Bello Capital, and has several San Diego-area properties. The post Breakthrough Properties, Tishman Speyer Provide $90M Mezz Loan for Life Science Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer co-invest $90M mezzanine bridge loan for life science campus.
Aperture Del Mar, 538k SF Class A lab/office, fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences through 2036.
Del Mar Heights, San Diego; loan refinances existing debt, part of Breakthrough's second life science fund.
stories.summary: Breakthrough Properties and Tishman Speyer jointly provided a $90 million mezzanine bridge loan for Aperture Del Mar, a newly constructed 538,000-square-foot Class A life science campus in San Diego's Del Mar Heights. The four-building complex is fully occupied by Neurocrine Biosciences through 2036. The loan refinances existing debt and is part of Breakthrough's second dedicated life science fund.
stories.impact: Validates San Diego's status as a major biopharmaceutical innovation hub with strong capital availability for class-A life science real estate. Neurocrine's long-term lease (12+ years remaining) and full occupancy demonstrate durable tenant demand and financing appetite. For multifamily developers in San Diego: thriving biotech ecosystem (Del Mar Heights, Torrey Pines, UTC) continues to attract skilled workforce; signals strong underlying housing demand in Premium/near-biotech submarkets; recommend close monitoring of vacant land and multifamily development capacity near major life science campuses.

stories.title: West Palm Beach Multifamily Property Converted From Condos Sells for $91M
stories.excerpt: The seesaw history of a West Palm Beach residential complex has a new chapter. A joint venture between the Kamson Corporation and Joel Gluck’s Scopus Property Management has closed on a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, Commercial Observer has learned. The 400-unit property was built in 1990 for multifamily usage and later converted to condominiums before it was restored back to rental housing in August 2025. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl supplied an $81 million acquisition loan for the property, which encompasses 28 acres on 1401 Village Boulevard. Previous ownership consisted of individual owners of the 400 condo units who decided to terminate the communities’ condominium association last year. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the debt with a team led by David Bollag and James Darling. “Ponte Verde is a well-located community with strong bones and a clear path forward,” Bollag said in a statement. “Rather than underwriting to where the property had been, [Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl’s] teams focused on the strength and experience of the buyer and the credibility of the business plan, which allowed us to deliver a financing solution on the timeline the transaction required.” The Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes multifamily community consists of 23 two- and three-story garden-style residential buildings totaling roughly 360,488 net rentable square feet, featuring one- and two-bedroom floor plans. Community amenities include a resident clubhouse, two swimming pools, a fitness center, tennis courts, racquetball courts, a sand volleyball court, a barbecue area and spa. Prospect Ridge, Blue Owl, the Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management acquire Ponte Verde for $90M in West Palm Beach.
400-unit community (28 acres), built 1990, condo-converted, restored to rental August 2025; $81M acquisition loan.
Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl financed; property undergoes moderate rehab and repositioning to rental.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Kamson Corporation and Scopus Property Management closed a $90 million acquisition of Ponte Verde at Palm Beach Lakes, a 400-unit multifamily community in West Palm Beach that was built as rentals in 1990, converted to condos, and restored to rental housing in August 2025. Prospect Ridge and Blue Owl provided an $81 million acquisition loan. The property sits on 28 acres and is undergoing rehab and repositioning.
stories.impact: Demonstrates strong capital availability for condo-to-rental conversions in South Florida submarkets, particularly when acquisition fundamentals are strong. West Palm Beach's full 400-unit conversion signals investor confidence in stabilized demand and pricing power post-repositioning. For TCR: opportunity to track similar condo conversions in secondary FL metros; rising acquisition prices and lender appetite for conversions suggest tightening supply and rental demand—potential signal to accelerate new-build deliveries in West Palm Beach and surrounding markets before land and labor costs rise further.

stories.title: Waste Management Buys 146-Acre Miami-Dade Development Site for $380M
stories.excerpt: Waste Management has paid nearly $380 million for about 146 acres in Medley, Fla., where the Houston-based company will likely build another landfill, property records show. The land sits parallel to Route 27 at 9515 Northwest 95th Avenue near the Everglades national park. About half the site remains vacant while the rest serves as a surface truck parking lot. The property sits adjacent to Waste Management’s 170-acre Medley Landfill complex. An entity tied to Hialeah Gardens-based Lowell Dunn Company sold the land. The same entity provided $366.8 million in seller financing, which is scheduled to mature in 2046. In a recorded easement, Lowell Dunn Company also agreed to allow Waste Management to install underground stormwater pipes across its neighboring property, enabling runoff from Waste Management’s site to discharge into a canal north of the property. Representatives for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The deal marks the second acquisition made by a waste management company in Miami-Dade County just this month. Woodlands, Texas-based Waste Connections paid $51 million for a 12-acre surface trucking parking lot in Miami Gardens. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Waste Management acquires 146-acre Medley, FL development site for $380M near Miami-Dade.
Land adjacent to existing 170-acre Medley Landfill; seller (Lowell Dunn Company) provided $366.8M financing through 2046.
Site includes 50% vacant land and truck parking; likely intended for landfill expansion.
stories.summary: Waste Management purchased approximately 146 acres in Medley, Florida for nearly $380 million, located adjacent to its existing 170-acre Medley Landfill complex and parallel to Route 27 near the Everglades. The seller, Lowell Dunn Company, provided $366.8 million in seller financing maturing in 2046. The site currently comprises vacant land and surface truck parking; WM likely plans landfill expansion. The seller also granted an easement for stormwater infrastructure.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, this large industrial/waste infrastructure investment in Medley signals continued logistics and industrial consolidation in Miami-Dade's western corridor. Indirectly, landfill expansion may constrain nearby residential development due to environmental/nuisance setbacks and reduce attractiveness of adjacent areas for multifamily—developers should flag Medley and western Dade as less favorable for residential infill and focus growth on eastern/central submarkets (Brickell, Wynwood, etc.).

stories.title: Carlyle Group, Haussmann Submit Plans for 99 Units at Brooklyn’s 566 Grand Avenue
stories.excerpt: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development have plans to partner on a 99-unit apartment complex in Brooklyn’s Crown Heights neighborhood. The two developers filed plans Thursday with the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) to bring a new 12-story mixed-use building to 566 Grand Avenue, near the corner of Grand Avenue and Bergen Street. Spokespeople for Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building will feature 99 Class A apartments, according to the filing, as well as ground-floor retail space. There will be 10 apartments on the second floor, 11 units each on the third through ninth floors, and four apartments each on floors 10, 11 and 12. The developers also plan to include several in-demand amenities at the property, such as a pet spa, a tenant theater, a game room, a children’s playroom, coworking space, a gym and an outdoor lounge. It is unclear if Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development plan to utilize the 485-x tax abatement program, which offers developers significant and lengthy tax breaks if their buildings feature a certain percentage of affordable housing. However, the 99-unit plan does provide a clue that this might be the case. A widely unpopular component of the 485-x program is higher construction wage requirements for buildings with 100 or more units. However, buildings with 99 or fewer units that utilize this program are not bound by those wage requirements. Crown Heights has been awash with residential building plans as of late. Avery Hall is planning an 18-story, 250-unit development at 1550 Bedford Avenue, while the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) is looking to build a 300-unit housing development in the neighborhood at 1119 Pacific Street. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development file DOB plans for 99-unit mixed-use at 566 Grand Avenue, Brooklyn.
12-story Class A building in Crown Heights; ground-floor retail; full amenity suite (pet spa, theater, coworking, gym).
Units range from studios to 2BR, distributed across floors 2–12; status of 485-x tax abatement unclear.
stories.summary: Carlyle Group and Haussmann Development filed plans with NYC DOB for a 99-unit Class A apartment complex at 566 Grand Avenue in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. The 12-story mixed-use building will include ground-floor retail and amenities (pet spa, tenant theater, game room, gym, coworking space, children's playroom, outdoor lounge). Unit mix spans studios to 2-bedroom apartments across floors 2–12. Tax incentive utilization status (485-x abatement) remains unclear.
stories.impact: Signals continued capital and development momentum in Brooklyn's Crown Heights/Prospect Heights corridor, particularly from major institutional developers (Carlyle, Haussmann). 99-unit scale and Class A finishes indicate strong renter demand and pricing power in the submarket. For TCR: Crown Heights remains competitive for new supply; recommend monitoring absorption and pricing of this project post-opening. If 485-x abatement is utilized, clarifies NYC's continued willingness to incentivize residential in outer-borough neighborhoods—consider similar projects in adjacent Williamsburg, Greenpoint, and Bed-Stuy submarkets.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Refis San Diego Apartments With $34M Loan

Lightstone Capital originated the senior loan for Svitak’s Kaya Apartments development in San Diego’s Bankers Hill neighborhood. John Zubak, managing director and head of origination, western region at Lightstone Capital, originated the deal. “From the outset, Kaya has been about creating housing that is deeply connected to the character of Bankers Hill while fostering a true sense of community,” Svitak said in a statement. Located at 2700 Third Avenue, Kaya Apartments debuted last year with 78 units ranging from studios to two bedrooms. Community amenities at the fully-leased complex include coworking space, community lounge, a shared kitchen and on-site café. Lightstone Capital also closed a $23.4 million senior bridge loan in July for Alliance Development Services‘ The Flats at TerraMar multifamily project in Carlsbad, Calif. Located at 5010 Avenida Encinas 32 miles north of San Diego, the 98-unit apartment community with 15 designated as affordable housing will involve converting a former Studio 6 hotel. Last but not least, Lightstone also recently originated a $11.5 million senior bridge loan for Fuller Realty‘s acquisition of an industrial property at 300 S. Sheldon Road in Channelview, Texas. bullets: Lightstone Capital originates $34.25M senior bridge loan for Kaya Apartments, San Diego (Bankers Hill).
78-unit newly completed property; fully leased; studios to 2BR; amenities include coworking, lounge, shared kitchen, café.
Developer Jeff Svitak; bridge debt typical for newly stabilized assets; similar Lightstone deal (Carlsbad) closed July.
stories.summary: Lightstone Capital originated a $34.25 million senior bridge loan for Kaya Apartments, a 78-unit newly completed multifamily development in San Diego's Bankers Hill neighborhood at 2700 Third Avenue. The property, which opened in 2024, is fully leased with studio to 2-bedroom units and amenities including coworking space, community lounge, shared kitchen, and on-site café. Developer Jeff Svitak is utilizing bridge debt to finance the stabilized asset; Lightstone also recently closed a similar $23.4 million bridge loan for a 98-unit Carlsbad property.
stories.impact: Demonstrates continued lender appetite for newly completed, fully-leased multifamily in San Diego submarkets (Bankers Hill, Carlsbad), even in higher-rate environment. Full leaseup at opening and bridge-loan availability signal strong demand absorption and investor confidence in Class A pricing. For TCR: San Diego remains attractive for newly delivered product; monitor Lightstone and other bridge lenders for permanent-debt refinance signals 12–18 months post-opening—could indicate rental-growth trajectory and cap-rate compression, informing future acquisition/development underwriting in Bankers Hill, UTC, and other premium San Diego corridors.

stories.title: Rexford Plans Up to $2B in Sales After Posting $507M Loss in Q2
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is dramatically accelerating its shift from being the most aggressive industrial buyer in Southern California into perhaps the region’s biggest seller. The Los Angeles-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has identified about $2 billion of “noncore assets” for disposition as it continues to prioritize keeping tenants in Rexford buildings. That property sales forecast is sharply up from the previous range of $400 million to $500 million. During the REIT’s earnings call Friday, CEO Laura Clark said the disposition pool encompasses about 8 million square feet with limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market — generally by more than 20 percent. Chief Financial Officer Michael Fitzmaurice said about $1 billion will repay debt maturing in 2027, rather than refinance into a higher rate environment. The remaining proceeds will be guided by market conditions. “We’re not de-levering to sit idle; we’re de-levering to redeploy,” Fitzmaurice said. The vast majority of Rexford’s property sales are expected to close before the end of the year. “We expect that pricing will be achieved at levels that allow us to redeploy proceeds on a neutral to accretive basis through our 2027 FFO per share, and this is not a dilutive exercise,” Clark said. Rexford said it sold seven properties totaling approximately 572,000 square feet for $137.9 million during the second quarter, after disposing of five properties for $127.4 million in the first quarter. The company previously known for 10-figure buying sprees has completed no acquisitions this year. Rexford plans to use property sales proceeds to repay debt, repurchase shares and pursue higher-yielding investments. It bought back $100 million of stock during the quarter, bringing its 2026 repurchases to $300 million, and its board subsequently authorized a new $1 billion repurchase program. bullets: Rexford Industrial increases noncore asset sale guidance from $400–500M to ~$2B; CEO Laura Clark announced Friday.
Disposition pool includes ~8M SF with limited value creation, short lease terms, rents >20% above market.
$1B allocated to 2027 debt repayment; remainder to redeploy capital as market conditions permit.
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty dramatically increased its noncore asset disposition guidance from $400–500 million to approximately $2 billion, representing a strategic shift from aggressive buyer to major seller in Southern California. The disposition pool comprises roughly 8 million square feet with limited value-creation potential, shorter lease terms, and rents substantially above market (typically >20%). CFO Michael Fitzmaurice noted that about $1 billion of proceeds will repay debt maturing in 2027, while remaining capital will be redeployed according to market conditions.
stories.impact: Signals capital recycling and potential deleveraging pressure in industrial REIT sector amid higher refinance rates and overvalued inventory. Rexford's aggressive shift from accumulation to disposition of above-market-rent assets suggests slowing industrial demand in SoCal and rising refinance risk for overleveraged portfolios. For TCR multifamily: Rexford's $2B fire sale of industrial assets may indicate broader SoCal real estate stress and capital flight; monitor for secondary effects on regional debt availability, cap rates, and land prices. If industrial REITs de-lever and liquidate, precedent for increased institutional trophy-asset sales and potential yield compression for multifamily, creating both refinance pressure and acquisition opportunity depending on market timing.
